headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network defaults can leak or corrupt shared work when paired with LangChain4j, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the lack of a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangChain4j has no documented I/O surfaces or shared channel, while Mentat reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout. That makes only manual copy-paste or file handoff plausible, so direct injection is not default. The pair still has a weak bridge through files and terminal text, but the pathway is not automatic.
conditions: IF an operator copies LangChain4j output into Mentat prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF Mentat is configured to ingest untrusted file content as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw model output into Mentat prompts.
Add a short human review step before any file handoff.
Use plain-text summaries instead of executable instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read and write files and has broad network egress, while LangChain4j is a library with no documented egress or file surfaces. If both touch the same workspace, Mentat can read source code and send it to its model provider; LangChain4j may also process content passed through it. The shared-file path exists in default Mentat usage, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree, Mentat can read files LangChain4j produced or touched.
IF Mentat sends selected file contents to its configured model provider, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only.
Disable or minimize file selection before model calls.
Review outbound requests from Mentat during runs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and modify_git_state with shared state via filesystem; LangChain4j is not runnable and exposes no write controls, so the conflict is one-sided but still dangerous. If LangChain4j-generated artifacts are fed into Mentat, Mentat can overwrite or commit them without locking. Uncertainty about LangChain4j’s runtime role does not reduce the filesystem collision risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout, Mentat can modify shared state without coordination.
IF LangChain4j is used to generate files that Mentat later edits, concurrent overwrites can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause Mentat before LangChain4j writes artifacts.
Require manual git review before commits.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional edit coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes diffs after user confirmation, so it can act on LangChain4j-produced text if the operator forwards it. LangChain4j itself is a library, not an autonomous verifier, so the main cascade is from generated content into Mentat’s edit proposals. The confirmation step reduces but does not eliminate propagation of bad facts or instructions.
conditions: IF LangChain4j output is treated as authoritative input to Mentat, errors can propagate into proposed diffs.
IF the operator approves Mentat diffs without independent verification, the cascade reaches the codebase.
mitigations: Verify LangChain4j outputs before handing them to Mentat.
Ask Mentat for diffs only, not direct execution.
Review every proposed patch line by line.
Limit tasks to low-risk files first.
requires-engineering: add automated validation before patch approval.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. LangChain4j is open-source and Mentat is open-source with model-provider API keys and outbound calls, so the only concrete compliance concern is operator-controlled data exposure through Mentat’s network use. Because the pair lacks a documented jurisdictional mismatch, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Mentat and the configured model provider is outside policy, compliance risk increases.
IF the operator requires residency guarantees that the model provider does not meet, the deployment becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Mentat sessions.
Check the configured model provider’s residency terms.
Rotate or restrict API keys to approved environments.
Log data-class decisions for each run.
requires-engineering: enforce provider allowlists and retention controls.
